segments.text: mutt - The Mutt Mail User Agent

Mutt is a small but very powerful text based program for reading and sending electronic mail under unix operating systems, including support for color terminals, MIME, OpenPGP, and a threaded sorting mode.

[[p0]]: This manual page gives a brief overview of the [[p1]] executable command line options. A copy of the full manual is located in [[p2]], in text, HTML, and/or PDF format. Please refer to the manual to learn how to use and configure Mutt.

The [[p0]] option must be placed at the end of command line options.
Specify a blind carbon copy (BCC) address.

If Mutt was compiled with [[p0]] log debugging output to [[p1]]. [[p2]] can range from -5 to 5 and affects verbosity. A value of zero disables debugging. A value less than zero disables automatic log file rotation; the log level is then its absolute value. A value of 2 (-2) is recommended for most diagnosis.
Print the value of all configuration options to stdout.
Edit the [[p0]] file specified by [[p1]] or [[p2]] file specified by [[p3]] during message composition.
Specify a configuration [[p0]] to be run after processing of initialization files.
Use [[p0]] instead of the user configuration file.
Display a short option summary and exit.

Specify a [[p0]] file which contains header and body to use to send a message. If [[p1]] is “[[p2]]”, then data is read from stdin. The draft file is expected to contain just an RFC822 email — headers and a body. Although it is not an mbox file, if an mbox "[[p3]]" line is present, it will be silently discarded. Draft files are processed the same in interactive and batch mode; they are not passed through untouched. For example, encrypted draft files will be decrypted.
Specify an [[p0]] file to be inserted into the body of a message. Ignored if [[p1]] is set. If [[p2]] is “[[p3]]”, then data is read from stdin.
Specify a default mailbox [[p0]] for newly created folders. Can be one of the following: mbox, MMDF, MH or Maildir. See also [[p1]] in the manual.
Do not read the system-wide Muttrc configuration file.
Resume a postponed message. Exit immediately if there are no postponed messages.
Query a configuration [[p0]]. The query is performed after all configuration files have been parsed, and any [[p1]] given on the command line have been executed.
Open a mailbox in read-only mode.
Specify the [[p0]] of the message. Must be enclosed in quotes if it contains spaces.
Display the Mutt version number and compile-time definitions.
Start Mutt with a listing of all mailboxes specified by the [[p0]] configuration command.
Exit immediately with code 1 if [[p0]] specified by [[p1]] does not contain any messages.
Open the first mailbox specified by the [[p0]] configuration command which contains new mail. Exit immediately with code 1 if there is no new mail in any of them.
Treat remaining arguments as [[p0]] even if they start with a dash. See also [[p1]] above. [[p2]] can be a local or network mail address as well as mailto: URL.
Specifies the editor to use when composing messages. If both EDITOR and VISUAL are set, VISUAL takes precedence. If neither EDITOR nor VISUAL are set, the default is [[p0]](1).
Paths used to initialize the random engine for SSL library.
Full path of the user's home directory.
Full path of the user's spool mailbox.
Full path of the user's spool mailbox if MAIL is unset. Commonly used when the spool mailbox is a [[p0]](5) folder.
Path to search for mailcap files.
If this variable is set, mailcap are always used without prompting first.
Directory in which the user's PGP public keyring can be found. When used with the original PGP program, mutt and [[p0]](1) rely on this being set.
Directory in which temporary files are created. If unset, [[p0]] is used for $tmpdir, and [[p1]] is used for $tmpdraftdir. See also the $tmpdir and $tmpdraftdir configuration variables.
Used to determine charset and locale to use.
Directory containing translation files. If set, this path overwrite the Mutt installation directory. Used for testing translation changes.
File containing debugging output. Log files are automatically rotated by [[p0]] changing the number at the end. See [[p1]] option above.
User definition for handling non-text MIME types.
System definition for handling non-text MIME types.
User's personal mapping between MIME types and file extensions.
System mapping between MIME types and file extensions.
None. Mutts have fleas, not bugs.
Suspend/resume while editing a file with an external editor does not work under SunOS 4.x if you use the curses lib in /usr/5lib. It [[p0]] work with the S-Lang library, however.
Resizing the screen while using an external pager causes Mutt to go haywire on some systems.
Suspend/resume does not work under Ultrix.
The help line for the index menu is not updated if you change the bindings for one of the functions listed while Mutt is running.

For a more up-to-date list of bugs, errm, fleas, please visit the mutt project's bug tracking system under https://gitlab.com/muttmua/mutt/issues. NOTE: The bug tracking system is not meant for feature requests. These should go to the mutt-dev mailing list, see section 1.2 Mailing Lists of the manual for details.
